input.instruction: Complete a loss-of-use review handoff. Staff must decide habitability and expense eligibility; the handoff is sufficiently specified for review, so unknown staff findings are not missing customer-form fields. Fill exactly the specified document fields from the supplied conversation and records. Normalize dates to ISO YYYY-MM-DD. Copy names, addresses, emails, and identifiers with the spelling supplied. This is an extraction-only task; actions must be empty. In the response distinguish drafting from execution.

messages.text: After smoke from the small fire on October 4, 2026, I spent two nights at a hotel. Can the loss-of-use part reimburse me?
Was your home declared uninhabitable, or did you choose the hotel while waiting for advice?
I left because the smell bothered me. Nobody has said whether 26 Spruce Court, Larkport, US was uninhabitable. I have not asked the building manager yet.
Which expenses are documented, and which are future plans?
The uploaded hotel receipt is $180 total for the two nights. My regular monthly rent is $1,000. I might book three more nights, perhaps another $270, but I have not booked or paid that.
What should staff clarify and where should they contact you?
Ask whether the home was actually uninhabitable from the covered fire and what expenses qualify. Contact ren.snow@post.example. Do not promise the rent or planned hotel will be reimbursed.

documented_hotel_expense.description: Already incurred hotel total supported by the supplied receipt, in USD.

ordinary_monthly_rent.description: Ordinary recurring rent reported by the customer, in USD; not an additional expense.

proposed_future_hotel_estimate.description: Customer estimate for unbooked future hotel expense, in USD.

habitability_confirmed.description: Whether the home is established as uninhabitable; null if not determined.

loss_of_use_limit.description: Issued loss-of-use limit in USD; not a payment promise.

reimbursement_approved.description: True only for authoritative reimbursement approval; false if record explicitly records no decision.
